note: Generated from the live registry, never hand-maintained. THREE INDEPENDENT AXES: representable (the model can express it), resolvable (the resolver turns it into explicit numbers), generatable (the geometry pipeline builds a solid for it). A capability may be representable and resolvable while remaining ungeneratable, and reporting that as 'supported' would be a misstatement. Multi-stone GEOMETRY is PARTIAL: the arrangement resolves every instance and the compilation boundary reports each one's generation status, but one stone component is emitted.

componentNaming.note: An additional instance's component is stone_reference.<instanceId>. The prefix is recognized by backend/jewelmind/geometry/roles.py, so such a component is classified as a stone reference and stays excluded from production exports by default (LAW-006) rather than falling through to the production_metal default.

capabilities.note: A first-class occurrence with a stable ID, a stone reference, a role, a placement and a gem. One instance is generated as the existing stone_reference component.
An instance placed by explicit XYZ plus a vertical-axis rotation. Resolved exactly; a non-zero XY offset is not yet built, because the current stone builder places one stone on the design axis.
Named groups with their own origin; a member's placement composes with the group transform during resolution.
count/spacing/direction, optionally centred on the anchor. Expanded to explicit member placements by closed-form evaluation.
count/radius/startAngle/sweep, optionally aligning each member to its radius. Expanded by closed-form evaluation.
One reflected copy across the YZ or XZ plane, flipping a chiral stone's own orientation.

A RELATIVE placement mode resolves against the parent group's frame. Placement relative to ANOTHER INSTANCE is PLANNED: it needs a dependency order, and a cyclic reference has no determinate resolution.
Five relation kinds are representable, reference-checked and preserved through resolution. They are DECLARATIONS, not constraints: nothing moves an instance to satisfy one. Enforcement is PLANNED.

The arrangement resolves every instance, and the compilation boundary reports each one's generation status. The current pipeline emits ONE stone component, so additional instances are reported NOT_GENERATED with a reason. See docs/bible/24-arrangement/execution-boundary.md.
scale and orientationDeg are representable and carried through resolution. Neither is applied to geometry yet, because doing so requires the multi-stone emission path.
Each instance may carry its own GemIdentity, resolved through the real Sprint 21 registry. Semantic only — it never affects geometry, exactly as for the single-stone case.
Tilt and roll. Deliberately not representable: accepting a rotation no builder can execute would be a silently ignored field.
Members distributed along an arbitrary curve. Needs curve evaluation, which belongs to Atlas, not to a declarative arrangement.
Iterative satisfaction of relations. Explicitly out of scope: a solver's output depends on iteration order and starting values, which this layer's determinism guarantee forbids.
Whether two placed stones overlap is a GEOMETRIC fact, answerable only by Geometry Inspection once multi-stone geometry exists. No spacing rule is invented here.
Minimum spacing, accent-to-centre proportion, pave density. Each needs sourced professional evidence this project does not have, so none exists.
